column1: # The matmul tables of the Metal backend: which multiply kernels exist, and how the work is divided per card and weight.
# A line that is exactly [name] starts a section; the next row is that section's header and is required as written.
# Cells are separated by one tab. - = absent. No file is read at run time: the generators below run when CMake configures.
# [tiles]: the batch route and the tiled kernel's work plan, per card and weight type, and every work plan the tiled
# kernel is compiled for. matmul/gen-tiles.cmake turns the rows into batch-routes-table.h (ggml_metal_batch_route_decide,
# matmul/batch-route.cpp), tiled-plan-table.h (ggml_metal_tiled_tune_load, matmul/tiled-plan.cpp), and the compiled plans:
# tiled-compiled-table.h and tiled-plans.metal (one compiled copy of the kernel per distinct set of the eleven values,
# every weight entry named <entry>_lay_<the eleven values>; the default plan first, then in the order a plan first appears).
# A row has one of three roles:
#   tuned: what was measured on one card for one weight type: its batch thresholds, its plan, or both.
#   default: the plan every card runs that has no tuned plan. Exactly one row.
#   candidate: a plan compiled so it can be measured (llama-metal-tiled-sweep), selected by no card yet.
# The plan of a card and weight: its tuned row for the type, else its tuned row for any, else the default. A tuned plan
# is used only when the card reports the wave width and group memory written in its row, and the plan passes the checks
# of ggml_metal_tiled_plan_check; else the default plan runs. The thresholds of a row do not depend on that check.
# GGML_METAL_KQ_EXT_ROWS=0 or GGML_METAL_KQ_HW_ROWS=0 in the environment ignores every threshold.
# To change a threshold: measure prompt speed on the card at the column counts around the change, write the numbers in
# route_source, leave column counts that were not measured on the route they had, run route_test on the card.
# To make a card run a plan: run llama-metal-tiled-sweep on it and add the row it prints. To try a new plan: add a
# candidate row; the build refuses values the kernel cannot run and names the condition.
# Columns
#   card: tuned rows: the card's name as Metal reports it, exactly: the text after "found device: " in the log of any run
#       on that card (for example: AMD Radeon Pro Vega 64). A name that differs by one character matches no card. Other rows: any.
#   weight: tuned rows: the weight type, a type of [formats], or any = every type (any is allowed only for a row with a
#       plan and no threshold). One row per card and weight. Other rows: any.
#   plan: the plan's name: <bm>x<bn>_t<threads>, then _<what else differs> when two plans share those three (s16 = 16 sums
#       per thread, w64 = 64-thread warp tiles). Lower-case letters, digits and _. One name per set of values. - on a
#       tuned row = the row holds thresholds only.
#   role: tuned | default | candidate.
#   ext_from: columns from which the small-batch kernel takes the op: 2 to 9, or - = the format's start (2, or 4 for K-quants). Only for a type that has a small-batch kernel.

#   tiled_from: columns from which the tiled kernel takes the op where it can run it, ahead of the small-batch kernel: a number from 2 (at most 9 digits), above ext_from, without a leading zero. - = the small-batch kernel keeps every count it takes, and the tiled kernel takes what is left above 8 columns. Only for a type that has a tiled kernel.
#   wave: tuned rows: threads of one wave on the card when the row was measured (the log line "probed simd_width"). Other rows: -.
#   group_bytes: tuned rows: bytes of threadgroup memory the card allows (MTLDevice maxThreadgroupMemoryLength). Other rows: -.
#       The plan of a tuned row must run on that shape: threads a whole number of wave, (bm + bn) * (bk / 2 + pad) * 8 bytes within group_bytes.
#   warp: threads of one warp tile, 1 to 1024; divides threads.
#   threads: threads per threadgroup, 1 to 1024; a whole number of the card's waves.
#   bm: output rows per threadgroup tile, 1 to 1024.
#   bn: output columns per threadgroup tile, 1 to 1024.
#   bk: K step, 32 (the block size the weight loaders are written for).
#   wm: output rows per warp tile, 1 to 1024.
#   wn: output columns per warp tile, 1 to 1024.
#   wmiter: row passes per warp tile, 1 to 8.
#   tm: rows of sums per thread per pass, 2 to 8, even.
#   tn: columns of sums per thread per pass, 1 to 16.
#   pad: float2 slots added to each buffer row, 0 to 64.
#       The eleven values from warp to pad are the fields of struct ggml_metal_tiled_plan (matmul/tiled-plan.h), in its
#       order; all are given with a plan and all are - without one. Whole numbers without a leading zero. At most 16 plans.
#   route_source: the measurement behind the thresholds: date, model, the numbers, which counts were not measured. Free text, no tab. - without a threshold.
#   route_test: the command that proves the thresholds on the card; required with a threshold. Free text, no tab. - without a threshold.
#   plan_source: tuned rows: the measurement behind the plan (date, the numbers with the plan and with the default). Other rows: why the plan is compiled. Free text, no tab. - without a plan.
#   plan_test: tuned rows: the command that proves the plan on the card; required with a plan. Free text, no tab. Other rows: -.
# [formats]: per-format facts of the matvec and matmul kernels, one row per weight type. matmul/gen-formats.cmake turns
# the rows into mv-formats-table.h, read through ggml_metal_mv_format (matmul/formats.h).
# To add a weight type: add its kernel instantiations in matmul/, then its row. A cell says yes only when that kernel exists.
#   weight ([formats]): the weight type, a ggml type name in lower case with K upper (for example q4_K, iq4_xs, f16). One row per type.
#   nsg: simdgroups per threadgroup, equal to N_SG_<type> in ggml-metal-impl.h (checked when the host code compiles). - = the geometry comes from the tensor (float types).
#   nr0: rows per rows_per unit, equal to N_R0_<type> in ggml-metal-impl.h (checked the same way). - together with nsg.
#   rows_per: the unit nr0 counts in: simdgroup | threadgroup.
#   smem: threadgroup memory of the matvec kernel: none | bytes (the bytes cell) | lane-floats (one float per lane) | row-sums.
#   bytes: the fixed threadgroup memory in bytes, a number from 1, when smem is bytes; else 0.
#   nr0_from_pipeline: yes | no. yes = the kernel takes its row count from the pipeline. A [matvec_shapes] row needs yes for its weight.
#   reduce_recompile_below_32: yes | no. yes = below simd width 32 the kernel is compiled again with the shared-memory reduce.
#   matvec: yes | no. A matvec kernel exists. no = the one-column route does not take the type.
#   ext: the small-batch kernel: no | small (taken from 2 columns) | kquant (taken from the card's column count, [tiles]).
#   tiled: yes | no. A tiled matmul loader exists. no = the tiled route does not take the type.
#   w64_fallback: yes | no. A width-64 kernel without simd intrinsics exists.
#   grouped: yes | no. The type joins a grouped matvec.
#   shape_rows: yes | no. The type takes per-shape rows.
#   act_bf16: yes | no. A kernel reads a bf16 activation with this weight type. no = the op is refused and runs on the CPU.

#   act_f16: the same for an f16 activation: yes | no | mm. mm = only the matrix kernel (kernel_mul_mm_<type>_f16) reads it, so the op is taken only where the matrix route takes it (matrix hardware, above the column threshold). Else it runs on the CPU.
#   ext_wide: yes | no. yes = on a card without matrix hardware the small-batch kernel takes any column count. no = it stops at 8 columns.
# [matvec_defaults]: per card, how the one-column (matvec) kernels run. matmul/gen-matvec.cmake compiles the rows in
# (matvec-rows.h); device/init.m reads the row of the card it runs on (ggml_metal_matvec_default_row_of). A cell that is
# - leaves the backend's default; a card with no row runs every default. One row per card.
# To change a cell: measure decode speed on the card with and without it, same output, and write the numbers in evidence.
#   simd_sum_w64_ok: yes | no | -. The simd reduction gave correct sums at wave width 64 on the card. For the reader: no code reads it.
#   mv_reduce: the tail of a matvec's row sum on the shared-memory path: serial | tree | - (serial).
#   f_scalar_w64: on | off | - (off). on = the f16 and bf16 scalar matvec runs at wave width 64 instead of the width-64 fallback.
#   mv_group: seq | off | - (off). seq = the 2 to 4 Q8_0 matvecs that read one activation run in one launch.
#   q8_load_bytes: bytes per weight load of the Q8_0 matvec: 1 | 4 (aligned words) | - (1).
#   q8_rows8_min: the smallest row count of a single Q8_0 matvec that runs 8 whole rows per simdgroup, a number above 0, or - = never.
#   q8_act_load_bytes: bytes per activation load of the Q8_0 matvec: 4 | 16 (two aligned loads per lane; needs q8_load_bytes 4) | - (4).
#   mv_group_red: on | off | - (off). on = the grouped K-quant matvec stores every row before the row sums.
#   evidence: [matvec_defaults]: the measurement behind each cell. Free text, no tab.
# [matvec_shapes]: per card and K-quant weight shape, how many rows a simdgroup works and in which loop form.
# matmul/gen-matvec.cmake compiles the rows in (matvec-rows.h, ggml_metal_hw_mv_rows); ggml_metal_mv_hw_row
# (matmul/dispatch.h) takes the first row of the card that fits the op, in file order, so a prep row stands before the
# row without prep for the same shape. A shape with no row runs the format's rows per simdgroup. The rows of one card
# stand together. GGML_METAL_KQ_HW_ROWS=0 ignores every row, GGML_METAL_KQ_PREP=0 the prep rows, GGML_METAL_KQ_COLS=0 the rows of 2 to 4 columns.
# wave and group_bytes are the card's shape when the row was measured, for the reader: no code compares them.
# To add a row: time the kernel on the card at that shape with each rows value, same bytes out, and write the numbers in source.
#   kind: single = one matvec of this weight | group = the grouped launch whose members all have this weight type and shape (only a type whose [formats] row says grouped yes).
#   k: the weight's input columns (its first dimension), a number above 0.

#   m: the weight's output rows (its second dimension), a number above 0. With 2 to 4 columns: a whole number of nr0 x nsg rows (nsg of [formats]), since the column kernel reads whole threadgroups of weight rows.
#   cols: activation columns in the launch: 1, or 2 to 4 = a decode batch of that many columns (kind single, q4_K or q6_K).

#   prep: on | off. on = the row applies only where the tensor's Q4_K block headers were unpacked at load (q4_K only), and names the tensor for that. A prep row stands before the row without prep for the same shape.
#   form: the loop form of a 2 to 4 column row, - with one column. a = activations held across the rows of a pass | w = weights
#       held, activations reloaded per row | ap, wp = the same with the weights kept packed | ha, hap = paired halves (each half
#       of a 64-thread wave works nr0 / 2 rows; 2 or 3 columns, nr0 from 2, wave 64 only), hap with the weights kept packed.
#   source: the measurement behind the row: the time before and after, the thread limit, that the bytes are the same. Free text, no tab.
#       In [matvec_shapes], weight is q4_K | q5_K | q6_K and nr0 is the rows per simdgroup: 1 | 2 | 4 | 8.
